facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is visibility. Backlog of USD 8,556.2 million is 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue, most of the Government Operations work is for the US Government, and the credit facility covenants (maximum leverage 4.00 times, minimum interest coverage 3.00 times) leave wide room against the 2.56x derived net multiple, with compliance reported at every date read. The view would soften if cash flow held up after the vendor timing benefit reverses, if the medical business sale closed at close to its headline value, or if EBITDA growth continued without new debt.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a more positive view is that the conduct on record is conservative: the 2025 acquisitions were accompanied by borrowings that the zero-coupon convertible notes later refinanced, the former revolver and term loan were replaced by a larger revolver maturing in 2030, covenant compliance was reported at every date, and dividends are small against operating cash flow. The view would improve if the executed documents showed tight limits on restricted payments and added debt, and if sale proceeds were applied to debt. It would worsen if further acquisitions were funded by revolver borrowings before the medical sale closes, if integration of Kinectrics or Precision Components Group slipped, or if appropriations delays hit the unfunded backlog. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is a strength and refinancing is a 2028 to 2030 task rather than a near-term risk. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is cash of USD 568.53 million plus USD 1,248.60 million available under the undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and the USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028 are covered by cash alone. Pro forma cash and net debt after the medical business sale agreed on 2026-07-31 are not established. Contractual interest on the notes is only USD 33.00 million a year, before revolver commitment fees, because 60.98% of principal is zero-coupon convertible notes due in 2030. Both senior notes can be redeemed at par at any time, which gives flexibility, but the revolver's 2030 maturity comes forward if unsecured debt due within 91 days exceeds the facility's EBITDA measure, unless net leverage is at or below 2.00x or liquidity is at least 125% of that debt, which for the convertible notes means USD 1,562.50 million; the agreement's definitions are not supplied. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is moderate and has eased from its peak, but it depends on how joint-venture income is treated. Gross debt over derived last-twelve-months EBITDA is 3.56x against 3.92x at FY2025, and net debt of USD 1.45 billion is 2.56x against 2.95x. Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the pending medical business sale are not established, and the EBITDA still includes the medical business and only one quarter of Precision Components Group. Equity income of joint ventures is 15.93% of that EBITDA, and without it gross leverage would be 4.23x and net leverage 3.04x, although joint-venture dividends of USD 201.54 million exceeded income of USD 181.65 million over FY2023 to FY2025, so the nine-month retention looks like timing rather than loss. The facility's maximum leverage covenant is 4.00x, rising to 4.50x for up to four quarters after a material acquisition, and compliance is reported at every date, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margin resilience is the weakest financial dimension: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points, from 18.49% in FY2023 to 15.79% over the last twelve months. Three things drove it. Commercial Operations, with a nine-month operating margin of 8.29% against 18.01% for Government Operations, grew 62.10%, largely on acquisitions, while Government Operations grew 3.26%, and two acquisitions supplied 52.95% of nine-month revenue growth. Segment margins also slipped in FY2025, with Government Operations at 16.80% against 18.45% in FY2023. Selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, and unallocated corporate costs rose USD 19.73 million in the nine months of 2026. The pressure may be easing: EBITDA margin was 13.73% in the fourth quarter of 2025, 15.96% in the first half of 2026 and 17.38% in the third quarter against 16.37% a year earlier, and the Government Operations margin was 19.2% against 15.8%. But the nine-month margin of 16.46% is still below the 16.95% of a year earlier, so one quarter is not yet a trend. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Free cash flow is solid and improving, but its conversion is flattered by supplier timing and the business is still investing heavily. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 372.32 million is 65.50% of EBITDA, up from 46.01% in FY2023, 54.62% in FY2024 and 57.49% in FY2025, and the nine-month payables inflow of USD 150.33 million was 33.28% of nine-month operating cash flow; if that inflow reversed, last-twelve-months free cash flow would be USD 221.99 million, or 39.05% of EBITDA. This narrows the reading in Financial foundation: the combined line for contracts in progress and advance billings was an outflow of USD 49.11 million in the nine months, so customer advances did not lift operating cash flow even though the advance billings balance rose, and supplier timing is the item that can reverse. Capital expenditure is 5.73% of revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and the issuer expects this heightened level to decline as expansion projects are largely complete. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy, not operations, is the main swing factor, because acquisitions absorb the cash and the facility lets leverage rise. Acquisitions used USD 186.11 million of net cash over the last twelve months after USD 535.15 million in FY2025, and the issuer says it is exploring more and would fund them with cash, debt, equity or a mix. Dividends of USD 97.95 million are 26.31% of last-twelve-months free cash flow, no shares were bought back in 2026 and USD 347.6 million of buyback authority remains. The pending medical sale is valued at up to USD 800 million, but the net assets held for sale are carried at USD 654.62 million and no significant gain or loss is expected, so creditors should not assume cash proceeds near the headline or that they will repay debt, and no leverage target is stated. facts.text: Claims outside the debt figure are manageable but can draw on liquidity. Pension and retiree medical plans were underfunded by USD 127.08 million at FY2025 and the issuer states underfunded plan obligations of about USD 149.0 million at 2026-09-30, although its Government contracts provide for recovery of pension contributions for the Government Operations plans. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Creditors' position in the capital structure is the largest open question. The revolver carries first-priority liens on certain assets, excluding some Government Operations subsidiaries, and the filings word its release differently: the annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report require investment grade ratings of BBB- from S&P or Baa3 from Moody's, while the second- and third-quarter reports require ratings from two of three agencies with a stable outlook, with no amendment disclosed. No source states whether the senior or convertible notes are secured or how they rank against the revolver, and guarantees come from wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, so Canadian operations, with 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment, and the joint ventures appear to sit outside them, although the guarantor list is not supplied. Structural priority and recovery cannot be assessed here. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a strong view is that earnings quality and cash flow are weaker than the headline multiples suggest. Margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points since FY2023, the 3.56x leverage multiple counts joint-venture income that was only partly paid in cash in the nine months, last-twelve-months cash conversion includes USD 150.33 million of payables timing, and the issuer is acquiring while the sale that could repay debt has unstated proceeds. The evidence for creditors is stronger on balance: backlog is 2.38x revenue, liquidity is 0.90x gross debt, the first maturity is 19 months away and cash alone covers it, and third-quarter margin recovered to 17.38%. facts.text: The credit's strengths start with the sole-source naval franchise: Government Operations produces most segment profit from one customer with limited competition, and a backlog of 2.38x revenue with a falling unfunded share turns that position into visible cash flow for debt service. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The weaknesses start with margin: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points as lower-margin commercial work, a dip in government margin and corporate costs grew, so each acquisition has added revenue faster than profit. Cash flow quality is the second weakness, because conversion of 65.50% leans on payables timing and capital expenditure still runs at 1.67x depreciation. Financial policy is the third, with acquisitions funded partly by debt, a covenant that allows 4.50x after a material acquisition and no stated leverage target. Dependence on one customer's appropriations, with USD 1,970.9 million of unfunded backlog, is the fourth, and exposure to fixed-price commercial contracts in Canada and the United States, whose margin is 8.29%, is the fifth. facts.label: Debt instruments and maturity wall
facts.text: Every debt instrument is listed below with its terms as the filings print them. The credit agreement sets a maximum consolidated total net leverage ratio of 4.00x, which may rise to 4.50x for up to four consecutive quarters after a material acquisition, and a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, both tested on a rolling four-quarter basis; the issuer reports compliance at 2026-09-30 and every earlier date but states no ratio, and both ratios use EBITDA and net debt as the agreement defines them, which differ from the derived EBITDA used here, so headroom is not calculable. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: BWX Technologies manufactures precision naval nuclear components, reactors and fuel for the US Government, manages government nuclear sites mainly through joint ventures, supplies commercial nuclear components and services, and, until the pending sale closes, makes medical radioisotopes. Government Operations was 73.37% of FY2025 segment revenue and 66.88% in the nine months of 2026 as Commercial Operations grew through Kinectrics and Precision Components Group. The US Government was 68% of FY2025 consolidated revenue against 76% in FY2024, and large utilities were 57% of Commercial Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026. Long-term, progress-billed government work and a backlog of 2.38x revenue support cash-flow visibility, debt service and liquidity preservation, but a small number of large projects drives results, the main customer controls timing through annual funding, and commercial activity follows nuclear outage and refurbishment cycles, mainly in Canada, so refinancing confidence would weaken mainly if appropriations and nuclear cycles turned down together. facts.text: The company is publicly listed with one class of common stock, no sponsor and no controlling holder named in the filings, so there is no sponsor extraction route, but the proxy statement that would name large holders and directors was not supplied. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is mostly recurring long-cycle work. Government Operations revenue follows national security spending and the Navy's procurement of submarines and carriers, and all three profiles in the March 2024 shipbuilding plan show sustained or higher nuclear-powered procurement. Most Government Operations contracts are fixed-price incentive contracts that reimburse allowable costs plus a fee, and 46.78% of Government Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026 was on that basis, with firm fixed-price at 34.31% and cost-plus at 18.85%, so pricing power is limited by cost-based contracting but revenue is protected by cost recovery and by termination terms. Commercial Operations is bid competitively, with 61.92% of its revenue on firm fixed-price contracts and 35.59% on time-and-materials, and it depends on utility outage and refurbishment timing. This qualifies the 74.81% share of segment revenue on fixed-price or fixed-price incentive contracts stated in Business & governance: the unreimbursed overrun exposure sits mainly in the 43.46% on firm fixed-price contracts, because the incentive contracts reimburse allowable costs. Backlog moved from USD 7,260.7 million at FY2025 to USD 8,650.8 million at 2026-03-31, USD 8,398.1 million at 2026-06-30 and USD 8,556.2 million at 2026-09-30, while the unfunded part moved from USD 2,151.3 million to USD 2,367.4 million, USD 2,256.4 million and USD 1,970.9 million, so funded backlog has grown 28.89% since FY2025. The unfunded share of backlog and the annual funding cycle make timing, not demand, the credit risk, and unexercised options of about USD 1,400 million are expected only in 2030 and 2035. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Cost of operations is 77.09% of FY2025 revenue against 75.14% in FY2023, and selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, so operating leverage has worked against margin as Commercial Operations, Kinectrics and corporate costs grew. Government contracts bill allowable costs under federal cost rules and use escalation clauses, but costs such as interest and some compensation are not billable, and the issuer says it cannot be sure it can mitigate all cost increases. Commercial fixed-price work leaves overruns with the company, the supply base includes single-source suppliers that could exert bargaining power, and roughly three in ten employees are union members. Government Operations margin dipped to 16.80% in FY2025 from 18.45% in FY2023 because revenue growth included USD 83.4 million from the timing of long-lead material procurements and integration and restructuring costs rose USD 13.1 million, and it recovered to 18.01% in the nine months of 2026. Margins can be defended under volume pressure in Government Operations, where the nine-month margin of 18.01% compares with 15.89% a year earlier excluding a USD 29.4 million favourable contract adjustment, but not with the same confidence in Commercial Operations, where the margin was 8.29% against 8.05% in FY2023 and 6.77% in FY2025. facts.label: Capital intensity and FCF conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditure was 5.73% of last-twelve-months revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and property under construction of USD 714.78 million at 2026-09-30 shows the expansion programmes still carrying large balances, although the issuer expects heightened spending to decline as these projects are largely complete. The issuer does not split maintenance from growth capital expenditure, so the flexibility to cut is not established, but the stated end of the expansion cycle is credible support for free cash flow. Cash taxes of USD 84.69 million over the last twelve months and cash interest of USD 41.08 million remain modest, pension contributions of about USD 12.7 million and USD 2.7 million are expected in 2026, and operating leases add about USD 9.08 million of payments in the next year. Seasonality matters: retainages build in the first and third quarters and are collected in the second and fourth, and the fourth quarter normally brings the highest operating cash flow, so the nine-month cash flow is not a full-year run rate. EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 65.50% over the last twelve months, but 39.05% if the payables inflow reverses, which is still positive after dividends. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is limited in Government Operations because of capital, licensing, classified designs and clearances, and the Navy fuel plant is the sole provider, which supports renewal and margin; in Commercial Operations competitors such as Framatome, Doosan and AtkinsRéalis bid for work and the margin is 8.29%. The threat of new entrants is low in naval work and moderate in commercial heavy components, where the issuer is the only North American heavy nuclear component manufacturer. Substitutes matter only commercially, where demand depends on the competitiveness of nuclear power against other energy sources. Buyer power is the central force: one customer is 88% of Government Operations revenue, can terminate for convenience and does not have to exercise options, though termination recovers costs and profit on work done. Supplier power is real because single-source suppliers could set price and terms on key materials, which would reduce margin before it reduced volume. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Policy and regulation are a primary credit driver and the other external factors are not. Appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdown risk set the timing of new awards and payments, the Department of Energy budget drives site-management contracts and their joint-venture income, and nuclear licensing and procurement rules shape both capacity and cost. Executive Order 14372 may restrict distributions by defense contractors that miss performance requirements. Currency is a secondary factor because Canadian operations hold 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment and the issuer hedges with forward contracts of USD 142.5 million notional maturing to December 2028. Tariffs and inflation in steel are noted by the issuer but are not quantified. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: The credit-supportive strengths are sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue, liquidity of USD 1.82 billion with no maturity before 2028, low cash interest from zero-coupon convertible debt and government cost recovery on contracts, pensions and decommissioning. The credit constraints are a margin that has fallen 2.70 percentage points, cash conversion helped by payables timing, an acquisition-led financial policy with no stated leverage target, concentration on one customer and unfunded backlog of 23.03%, and unseen executed documents that leave ranking and covenant definitions unknown. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are sale proceeds applied to debt, the end of the heightened capital expenditure cycle, a sustained recovery in margin of the kind seen in the third quarter, and conversion of unfunded to funded backlog, which has already lifted funded backlog 28.89% since FY2025. Threats that could weaken credit quality are a debt-funded acquisition or revolver draw that returns leverage above its FY2025 peak, a continuing resolution or shutdown that delays awards and collections, cost overruns on fixed-price commercial work, and a failed or low-value medical sale. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The main credit supports are scale of USD 3.60 billion of last-twelve-months revenue, sole-source government demand, liquidity of 0.90x gross debt and a distant maturity profile; the main constraints are the margin trend, cash conversion that depends on supplier timing, and an acquisition-led policy whose limits are not documented in the filings supplied. The trend is improving on leverage, with gross leverage down from 3.92x at FY2025 to 3.56x and EBITDA growth of 10.66% over FY2025 in the last twelve months, but deteriorating on margin, and the third quarter suggests stabilisation. Interest cover is high at 13.84x on last-twelve-months cash interest and 17.22x on the contractual interest due in a year. Access to capital markets was shown by the USD 1,250 million convertible issue of 2025, and the only price evidence supplied is the quarter-end fair value of 96.50% of principal for the 2028 senior notes, 95.08% for the 2029 notes and 87.36% for the convertible notes, which does not by itself show stress but is not a market test. The key missing datapoints are the executed documents, the proceeds of the medical sale, the contract-level fixed-price exposure, a rating and market prices. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are funded backlog growth of 28.89% in the nine months of 2026, recognition of about 46% of backlog by the end of 2027, a Navy plan that sustains nuclear procurement, an expected fall in capital expenditure, the third-quarter margin recovery and low cash interest; the headwinds are the fiscal-year funding cycle, integration of Kinectrics, whose controls will be assessed for FY2026, and of Precision Components Group, whose price allocation is preliminary, the pending sale's timing in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, and reversal of payables timing. The 2028 notes become a current liability in 2027, but they are covered by cash. Over three to five years the issues are the 2028, 2029 and 2030 maturities, the convertible notes becoming redeemable from 2028-11-06, the revolver's early-maturity test before the 2030 convertible notes fall due, and the award of unexercised options in 2030 and 2035; the Commercial Operations outlook depends on nuclear utility spending and Canadian refurbishment, and the Government Operations outlook on appropriations. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario that fits this capital structure combines three events. Appropriations for the next federal year are delayed under a continuing resolution while a shutdown risk lingers, new awards slip, and retainage collections and joint-venture dividends that normally arrive in the fourth quarter are delayed. At the same time a fixed-price commercial project overruns and the vendor payments deferred in 2026 are paid, which removes the USD 150.33 million payables inflow. Revenue in Government Operations, which earns 81.43% of segment profit, would fall little because funded backlog is USD 6,585.3 million, but fixed costs of the expanded facilities would be absorbed over fewer awards, so the margin would fall below the nine-month level of 16.46% and last-twelve-months free cash flow would fall towards USD 221.99 million. Liquidity would hold: liquidity of USD 1.82 billion covers 5.39 years of cash interest, capital expenditure and dividends, in total USD 337.34 million a year, even with no operating cash flow at all. The leverage consequence would come from management choices, because a revolver draw for an acquisition before the medical sale closes would lift gross debt from USD 2.02 billion while EBITDA fell. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, and the observable triggers are a fall in funded backlog, a revolver draw, payables falling from USD 281.64 million and a margin below 16.46%. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, BWX Technologies presents a strong business profile supported by sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue and a long maturity runway, but credit quality is constrained by a falling EBITDA margin, an acquisition-led financial policy and unseen debt documents. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because conversion of 65.50% is helped by payables timing and capital expenditure remains high. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 and 2029 senior notes being repaid from cash and cash flow or refinanced at par, and on the 2030 convertible notes being addressed before the revolver's early-maturity test applies. The primary downside path is debt-funded acquisitions and margin erosion while government cash timing slips. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, the proceeds and use of the medical sale, contract-level fixed-price data, a rating and market prices. Top risk: acquisition-led leverage. Basis: calculation D21; calculation D54; calculation D05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for BWX Technologies, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is consolidated figures for FY2024, FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, carrying-value debt, liquidity, derived last-twelve-months measures and post-balance-sheet events.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is moderate and cash-backed, but the 3.56x gross and 2.56x net multiples of last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30 are flattered by working-capital timing and equity income, so creditors should rely on the long maturity runway rather than the multiple.

Gross debt is USD 2.02 billion, almost all fixed-rate or zero-coupon, with nothing due before 2028 and the USD 1,250 million revolver undrawn. EBITDA covered cash interest 13.84x over the last twelve months against 7.88x in FY2025, because the zero-coupon convertible notes replaced bank debt. The medical business sale of up to USD 800 million is pending and net debt after closing is not established.

Basis: calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C21; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16
### Key findings

Leverage peaked at the end of FY2025 and has eased since. Gross debt over derived EBITDA was 2.26x at FY2024, 3.92x at FY2025 and 3.56x at 2026-09-30, and net debt over EBITDA was 2.10x, 2.95x and 2.56x. Gross debt almost doubled in FY2025 as the convertible notes and the Kinectrics purchase were financed, and EBITDA growth has since absorbed part of it.

Basis: calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C22; calculation C23; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 80–81; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111

Interest cover improved sharply because the main new debt carries no coupon. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.44x in FY2024, 7.88x in FY2025 and 13.84x over the last twelve months, and the issuer's own schedule puts contractual interest due within a year at USD 33.0 million, which last-twelve-months EBITDA covers 17.22x. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months of USD 41.1 million still includes pre-refinancing months, so run-rate cover is higher than the last-twelve-months figure.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C30; calculation C49; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73

Earnings quality needs care because EBITDA includes equity income of joint ventures. That income is 15.93% of last-twelve-months EBITDA and was only partly received in cash: income of investees net of dividends was a USD 31,573 thousand deduction from operating cash flow in the nine months of 2026, which means the joint ventures retained more than they paid out.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

Cash generation looks stronger than it is. Last-twelve-months operating cash flow equals 101.81% of EBITDA for a business spending 5.73% of revenue on capital expenditure, because accounts payable rose USD 150,334 thousand on vendor payment timing and advance billings rose USD 123,057 thousand to USD 428.3 million. Free cash flow of USD 372.3 million over the last twelve months is therefore partly borrowed from suppliers and customers and can reverse.
Basis: calculation C31; calculation C41; calculation C48; calculation C50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

Liquidity is strong and the first maturity is distant. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is 0.90x gross debt, the revolver has USD 1,248.6 million available after letters of credit, and the first maturity is the USD 400 million senior notes due in 2028, which cash on hand already covers.
Basis: calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112

The convertible notes behave like straight debt. The conversion price of about USD 262.51 a share is far above the USD 152.39 average price paid for shares withheld in September 2026, and the notes' fair value of USD 1,092.0 million sits below their USD 1,250.0 million principal, so creditors should expect to be repaid in cash and no equity credit is warranted.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

Claims outside the debt figure are modest against EBITDA but real. Pension and retiree medical plans were underfunded by USD 127.1 million at FY2025, the quarterly report states underfunded plan obligations of approximately USD 149.0 million at 2026-09-30, surety bonds of USD 361.0 million and bilateral letters of credit of USD 37.6 million are contingent, and no purchase commitments, factoring or supply-chain finance are described.
Basis: calculation C34; calculation C46; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44

The medical business is already separated as held for sale, with assets of USD 700.4 million, but the benefit to creditors depends on proceeds that are not stated. The agreement values the business at up to USD 800 million, the closing is expected in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, and the part of EBITDA it contributes is not stated.
Basis: calculation C32; calculation C47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is visibility. Backlog of USD 8,556.2 million is 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue, most of the Government Operations work is for the US Government, and the credit facility covenants (maximum leverage 4.00 times, minimum interest coverage 3.00 times) leave wide room against the 2.56x derived net multiple, with compliance reported at every date read. The view would soften if cash flow held up after the vendor timing benefit reverses, if the medical business sale closed at close to its headline value, or if EBITDA growth continued without new debt.

The view would harden if the revolver were drawn for an acquisition, if advance billings or vendor payables unwound while EBITDA stalled, if the sale failed to close, or if a rating action changed the lien position of the credit facility.
Basis: calculation C37; calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Limitations

- EBITDA is derived because the issuer states none, so every leverage and cover multiple depends on operating income plus depreciation and amortization; an issuer-adjusted figure could move the multiples in either direction.
- Covenant headroom is not computed because the credit agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied, so the statement that covenants leave room rests on the reported compliance alone.

- The 2026-09-30 balance sheet separates the medical business as held for sale and earlier balance sheets are not recast, so comparisons of assets and liabilities with year-end mix the reclassification with trading.
- The maturity ladder is drawn at 2025-12-31 because the latest report gives no principal total, so a change in principal since then is not visible except that no borrowings were reported.
- No source states the legal rank or security of the senior notes or convertible notes, so the debt stack shows the revolver only and no structural or recovery conclusion should lean on it.

## Gaps

The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA in any filing read, so EBITDA is derived for every period and the bridge from reported to adjusted EBITDA is empty. This restricts comparison with issuer-defined and covenant measures. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the third-quarter 2026 earnings release with its reconciliation.

The cash flow statements print a dash instead of an amount for acquisitions, securities sales, short-term debt payments, convertible proceeds, issuance costs and capped calls in FY2024, and for securities sales, borrowings, repayments and share repurchases in the nine months of 2026. These cells are shown as not supplied rather than zero and restrict nothing, because the activity subtotals tie. Severity: Low. Action: none.

The quarterly reports print fewer cash flow lines than the annual report: deferred income taxes, short-term debt payments, convertible proceeds, issuance costs and capped calls. Those nine-month cells are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: read the next annual report.

The balance sheets do not print held-for-sale lines before 2026-09-30, and the latest balance sheet prints no current maturities of long-term debt line, so those cells are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none.

No principal total and no aggregate of deferred issuance costs are stated at 2026-09-30, so the difference of -28.117 USD millions between carrying value and the notes' principal at that date is not itemised and the debt reconciliation is drawn at 2025-12-31. This restricts reading of leverage on principal at the latest date. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the debt note of the next annual report.

Per-instrument carrying values are not disclosed at any date, and the terms of the other debt of 1.967 USD millions at 2025-12-31 are not stated at 2026-09-30. This restricts the instrument register to principal. Severity: Low. Action: none.

No source states the legal rank or security of the senior notes due 2028 and 2029 or the convertible notes due 2030, so they are left out of the debt stack and their ranking is not supplied in the instrument register. This restricts structural priority and recovery work. Severity: High. Action: supply the three indentures.
The amortisation schedule of the revolver is not stated. This restricts nothing for the snapshot. Severity: Low. Action: supply the credit agreement.

The credit agreement's EBITDA definition and the issuer's own covenant ratios are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not computed. This restricts any statement of headroom beyond the printed levels and the reported compliance. Severity: High. Action: supply the credit agreement and the compliance certificate.

The net proceeds, tax, retained stake and closing date of the medical business sale are not stated, so no pro forma net debt or leverage is stated. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the transaction announcement or closing report.

The 2026 reports give the US Government share of Government Operations revenue and nine-month segment margins, not the share of consolidated revenue or last-twelve-months margins, so those KPI cells are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none.

Leverage is stated at two year-ends and at 2026-09-30 only; the first two quarter-ends of 2026 are not stated, which restricts reading of the path within the year. Severity: Low. Action: extend the series from the first and second quarter reports.
The full-year contribution of Kinectrics to FY2025 EBITDA is not stated, so FY2025 leverage is not a pro forma figure. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the acquisition pro forma disclosure if wanted.

## Findings
### Bottom line

BWX Technologies, Inc. gives creditors unusually durable demand from a limited-competition supplier to the US naval nuclear programme, but its recent and pending portfolio moves make financial policy, not the business, the main creditor risk.

The US Government was 68% of FY2025 revenue and backlog of USD 8,556.2 million covers 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder is disclosed, but the proxy statement that would name large holders and directors was not supplied. Three acquisitions since January 2025 and a pending sale of the medical business for up to USD 800 million are reshaping the group, and no document supplied establishes the limits on that policy.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C03; calculation C04
### Key findings

Demand is durable but concentrated and appropriation-dependent. Government Operations carried 76% of backlog at FY2025, the US Government was 68% of revenue against 76% a year earlier, and USD 1,970.9 million of backlog, 23.03% of the total, is unfunded US Government work that depends on future appropriations. The issuer describes competition for naval nuclear components and fuel as limited and its Navy fuel plant as the sole provider, which supports renewal odds but ties creditor cash flow to one customer's budget cycle.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C01

The mix is moving toward Commercial Operations and Canada, which earn lower margins and carry more fixed-price risk. Commercial Operations rose to 26.63% of segment revenue in FY2025 from 19.36% in FY2024 as Kinectrics joined, its operating margin was 6.77% against 16.80% for Government Operations, 74.81% of nine-month 2026 revenue is fixed-price or fixed-price incentive work, and Canada holds 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment. A cost overrun on a fixed-price utility contract would reach cash flow before any covenant moves.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

Ownership is public and widely held, so no sponsor can extract value, but nothing supplied limits financial policy. The annual report defers directors, executive pay and large holders to a proxy statement that was not supplied. The signatories for chief financial officer and chief accounting officer changed between the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and one fewer director signed, with no reason stated, so succession and board change are noted but not assessed.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 142–143; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148

Shareholder distributions are moderate against cash flow, and acquisitions are the larger call on cash. Dividends and buybacks took 25.52% of FY2025 operating cash flow, the quarterly dividend was raised by 8.00% in 2026, no shares were repurchased under the buyback programme in the nine months of 2026 and USD 347.6 million of buyback authorisation remains, whereas acquisitions used USD 535.1 million of cash in FY2025 and USD 187.0 million in the nine months of 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C21; calculation C22

Acquisition appetite is explicit and integration is unfinished. Management says it is exploring further acquisitions and would fund them with cash, debt, equity or a mix. Kinectrics, bought in May 2025, is still being brought into internal controls and the auditor flagged its fair value as a critical audit matter, the Precision Components Group price allocation is preliminary, and unallocated corporate costs rose by USD 19.7 million in the nine months of 2026 on acquisition, restructuring and healthcare costs. Integration cost or overpayment would reduce the cash available for debt service.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46

The medical sale helps creditors only if proceeds reduce debt, which is not established. The agreement values the business at up to USD 800 million, BWXT keeps a minority interest, closing is expected in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, no significant gain or loss is expected, and the filings do not say what the proceeds will fund. Property, plant and equipment of USD 482.1 million sits in the held-for-sale assets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

Joint-venture earnings are cash in some periods and retained in others, and the contract base is turning over. Dividends received from joint ventures of USD 94.3 million exceeded equity income of USD 74.9 million in FY2025, but in the nine months of 2026 equity income, 20.40% of operating income, exceeded dividends. The Portsmouth, SACOM and West Valley Phase 1 contracts ended in 2025 and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and Canadian National Laboratory contracts began in late 2025, so income depends on renewals and performance scores.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C18; calculation C23; calculation C24

Legacy and contingent exposures are small in the filings but not capped by them. Asbestos liabilities of former subsidiaries were assumed by Babcock and Wilcox Enterprises at the 2015 spin-off and are channelled to a trust, although the filings concede possible underinsured exposure; the Department of Energy covers substantially all decommissioning costs of the two licensed US facilities, and the latest quarterly report states no material contingencies.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring operations but not for assessing creditor protections. The statements are audited by Deloitte and Touche LLP, controls are reported effective and covenant compliance is stated at every date, but the credit agreement, the indentures and the August 2026 supplemental indentures are not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, add debt or release liens is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 138–141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a more positive view is that the conduct on record is conservative: the 2025 acquisitions were accompanied by borrowings that the zero-coupon convertible notes later refinanced, the former revolver and term loan were replaced by a larger revolver maturing in 2030, covenant compliance was reported at every date, and dividends are small against operating cash flow. The view would improve if the executed documents showed tight limits on restricted payments and added debt, and if sale proceeds were applied to debt. It would worsen if further acquisitions were funded by revolver borrowings before the medical sale closes, if integration of Kinectrics or Precision Components Group slipped, or if appropriations delays hit the unfunded backlog.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45
### Limitations
- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no holder controls the company and the description of the board rest on the filings' silence and signature pages.
- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the conclusion on financial policy rests on documented conduct and not on what the documents permit.

- The sale agreement and the Precision Components Group allocation are known only from summaries, so the view of the portfolio reshaping may change once proceeds, the retained stake and the final goodwill are known.
- Joint-venture data is combined for all ventures, so the quality of equity income is judged from totals and not from individual contracts.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In November 2025 the company entered a second amended and restated credit agreement with a USD 1,250 million senior secured revolver maturing in 2030, issued USD 1,250 million of 0% convertible senior notes due 2030, used the proceeds to repay the former revolving credit facility and term loan, and paid USD 131.9 million for capped call transactions. The notes settle principal in cash, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 262.51 a share, and are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the credit facility. The USD 400 million senior notes due 2028 and 2029 carry 4.125% coupons and remain outstanding.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–42

The group bought Aerojet Ordnance Tennessee, Inc. for about USD 101.1 million in January 2025, Kinectrics for a headline price of CAD 782.7 million in May 2025 (purchase consideration of USD 440.6 million after assumed pension liabilities and debt), and Precision Components Group, LLC for about USD 216.8 million on 2026-07-01 under an agreement dated 2026-04-20. In the first nine months of 2025 net borrowings of USD 450.6 million accompanied the first two.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_bwxt_bwxt-63026x10qdocument.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C20

On 2026-07-31 the company agreed to sell its medical business, BWXT Medical and the stable medical isotope business of Kinectrics, to Nordic Capital in a transaction valued at up to USD 800 million, keeping a minority interest and continuing to supply isotope and radiochemical expertise. Completion is expected in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. Three supplemental indentures dated 2026-08-07 are listed as exhibits to the latest quarterly report, and their terms are not stated in the documents supplied.

Fundamental credit synthesis for BWX Technologies, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated business and financial profile through the quarter ended 2026-09-30, built on the five filings and the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

## Findings
### Bottom line

BWX Technologies combines a strong, sole-source naval nuclear franchise with adequate financial metrics, so creditors face little operating or liquidity risk before 2028 and the main risk is acquisition-led financial policy. Backlog of USD 8,556.2 million is 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue, liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is 0.90x gross debt of USD 2.02 billion, and the first maturity is USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation D21; calculation D29; calculation D30; calculation D31

Two limits qualify that view. The EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points since FY2023 to 15.79% over the last twelve months, and the proceeds of the pending medical business sale, the executed debt documents, ratings and prices were not supplied, so ranking, covenant headroom, pro forma debt and market pricing are not established.
Basis: calculation D05; calculation D06; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

The business is the strongest support: sole-source US naval nuclear demand gives creditors visible revenue that a competitor cannot easily take. Government Operations earned 81.43% of segment operating income in the nine months of 2026 on 66.88% of segment revenue, 88% of that revenue came from the US Government, and the issuer calls its Navy fuel plant the sole provider and competition limited. Backlog cover rose from 1.79x revenue at FY2024 to 2.38x, and the unfunded share of backlog fell from 29.63% at FY2025 to 23.03%. The exposure is one customer's annual appropriation cycle, so a continuing resolution or shutdown would delay awards and cash timing before it threatened repayment, and on termination the contracts generally allow recovery of costs and profit on work done.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2024-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation D11; calculation D12; calculation D21; calculation D22; calculation D23; calculation D24; calculation D80

Liquidity is a strength and refinancing is a 2028 to 2030 task rather than a near-term risk. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is cash of USD 568.53 million plus USD 1,248.60 million available under the undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and the USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028 are covered by cash alone. Pro forma cash and net debt after the medical business sale agreed on 2026-07-31 are not established. Contractual interest on the notes is only USD 33.00 million a year, before revolver commitment fees, because 60.98% of principal is zero-coupon convertible notes due in 2030. Both senior notes can be redeemed at par at any time, which gives flexibility, but the revolver's 2030 maturity comes forward if unsecured debt due within 91 days exceeds the facility's EBITDA measure, unless net leverage is at or below 2.00x or liquidity is at least 125% of that debt, which for the convertible notes means USD 1,562.50 million; the agreement's definitions are not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D28; calculation D29; calculation D38; calculation D39; calculation D40; calculation D75

Leverage is moderate and has eased from its peak, but it depends on how joint-venture income is treated. Gross debt over derived last-twelve-months EBITDA is 3.56x against 3.92x at FY2025, and net debt of USD 1.45 billion is 2.56x against 2.95x. Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the pending medical business sale are not established, and the EBITDA still includes the medical business and only one quarter of Precision Components Group. Equity income of joint ventures is 15.93% of that EBITDA, and without it gross leverage would be 4.23x and net leverage 3.04x, although joint-venture dividends of USD 201.54 million exceeded income of USD 181.65 million over FY2023 to FY2025, so the nine-month retention looks like timing rather than loss. The facility's maximum leverage covenant is 4.00x, rising to 4.50x for up to four quarters after a material acquisition, and compliance is reported at every date, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D33; calculation D34; calculation D35; calculation D36; calculation D37; calculation D42; calculation D44; calculation D45; calculation D46; calculation D47; calculation D48; calculation D75

Margin resilience is the weakest financial dimension: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points, from 18.49% in FY2023 to 15.79% over the last twelve months. Three things drove it. Commercial Operations, with a nine-month operating margin of 8.29% against 18.01% for Government Operations, grew 62.10%, largely on acquisitions, while Government Operations grew 3.26%, and two acquisitions supplied 52.95% of nine-month revenue growth. Segment margins also slipped in FY2025, with Government Operations at 16.80% against 18.45% in FY2023. Selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, and unallocated corporate costs rose USD 19.73 million in the nine months of 2026. The pressure may be easing: EBITDA margin was 13.73% in the fourth quarter of 2025, 15.96% in the first half of 2026 and 17.38% in the third quarter against 16.37% a year earlier, and the Government Operations margin was 19.2% against 15.8%. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a strong view is that earnings quality and cash flow are weaker than the headline multiples suggest. Margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points since FY2023, the 3.56x leverage multiple counts joint-venture income that was only partly paid in cash in the nine months, last-twelve-months cash conversion includes USD 150.33 million of payables timing, and the issuer is acquiring while the sale that could repay debt has unstated proceeds. The evidence for creditors is stronger on balance: backlog is 2.38x revenue, liquidity is 0.90x gross debt, the first maturity is 19 months away and cash alone covers it, and third-quarter margin recovered to 17.38%.

### Strengths and weaknesses

The credit's strengths start with the sole-source naval franchise: Government Operations produces most segment profit from one customer with limited competition, and a backlog of 2.38x revenue with a falling unfunded share turns that position into visible cash flow for debt service. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion and no maturity before 2028 mean that no refinancing is needed in the next 19 months, and cash interest of about USD 33.00 million a year follows from zero-coupon convertible notes that make up 60.98% of principal. Government contracts that reimburse allowable costs, recover pension contributions and cover decommissioning for two facilities shield the company from part of the cost of inflation and legacy liabilities, and the issuer showed capital market access when it placed USD 1,250 million of convertible notes in 2025.

### Company description

BWX Technologies manufactures precision naval nuclear components, reactors and fuel for the US Government, manages government nuclear sites mainly through joint ventures, supplies commercial nuclear components and services, and, until the pending sale closes, makes medical radioisotopes. Government Operations was 73.37% of FY2025 segment revenue and 66.88% in the nine months of 2026 as Commercial Operations grew through Kinectrics and Precision Components Group. The US Government was 68% of FY2025 consolidated revenue against 76% in FY2024, and large utilities were 57% of Commercial Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026. Long-term, progress-billed government work and a backlog of 2.38x revenue support cash-flow visibility, debt service and liquidity preservation, but a small number of large projects drives results, the main customer controls timing through annual funding, and commercial activity follows nuclear outage and refurbishment cycles, mainly in Canada, so refinancing confidence would weaken mainly if appropriations and nuclear cycles turned down together.

Financial policy is moderate in conduct, with dividends at 26.31% of last-twelve-months free cash flow and no 2026 buybacks, but there is no stated leverage target, management says it is exploring acquisitions, and the covenant allows 4.50x after a material acquisition. ### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mostly recurring long-cycle work. Government Operations revenue follows national security spending and the Navy's procurement of submarines and carriers, and all three profiles in the March 2024 shipbuilding plan show sustained or higher nuclear-powered procurement. Most Government Operations contracts are fixed-price incentive contracts that reimburse allowable costs plus a fee, and 46.78% of Government Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026 was on that basis, with firm fixed-price at 34.31% and cost-plus at 18.85%, so pricing power is limited by cost-based contracting but revenue is protected by cost recovery and by termination terms. Commercial Operations is bid competitively, with 61.92% of its revenue on firm fixed-price contracts and 35.59% on time-and-materials, and it depends on utility outage and refurbishment timing. This qualifies the 74.81% share of segment revenue on fixed-price or fixed-price incentive contracts stated in Business & governance: the unreimbursed overrun exposure sits mainly in the 43.46% on firm fixed-price contracts, because the incentive contracts reimburse allowable costs. Backlog moved from USD 7,260.7 million at FY2025 to USD 8,650.8 million at 2026-03-31, USD 8,398.1 million at 2026-06-30 and USD 8,556.2 million at 2026-09-30, while the unfunded part moved from USD 2,151.3 million to USD 2,367.4 million, USD 2,256.4 million and USD 1,970.9 million, so funded backlog has grown 28.89% since FY2025. The unfunded share of backlog and the annual funding cycle make timing, not demand, the credit risk, and unexercised options of about USD 1,400 million are expected only in 2030 and 2035.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of operations is 77.09% of FY2025 revenue against 75.14% in FY2023, and selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, so operating leverage has worked against margin as Commercial Operations, Kinectrics and corporate costs grew. Government contracts bill allowable costs under federal cost rules and use escalation clauses, but costs such as interest and some compensation are not billable, and the issuer says it cannot be sure it can mitigate all cost increases. Commercial fixed-price work leaves overruns with the company, the supply base includes single-source suppliers that could exert bargaining power, and roughly three in ten employees are union members. Government Operations margin dipped to 16.80% in FY2025 from 18.45% in FY2023 because revenue growth included USD 83.4 million from the timing of long-lead material procurements and integration and restructuring costs rose USD 13.1 million, and it recovered to 18.01% in the nine months of 2026. Margins can be defended under volume pressure in Government Operations, where the nine-month margin of 18.01% compares with 15.89% a year earlier excluding a USD 29.4 million favourable contract adjustment, but not with the same confidence in Commercial Operations, where the margin was 8.29% against 8.05% in FY2023 and 6.77% in FY2025.

### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital expenditure was 5.73% of last-twelve-months revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and property under construction of USD 714.78 million at 2026-09-30 shows the expansion programmes still carrying large balances, although the issuer expects heightened spending to decline as these projects are largely complete. The issuer does not split maintenance from growth capital expenditure, so the flexibility to cut is not established, but the stated end of the expansion cycle is credible support for free cash flow. Cash taxes of USD 84.69 million over the last twelve months and cash interest of USD 41.08 million remain modest, pension contributions of about USD 12.7 million and USD 2.7 million are expected in 2026, and operating leases add about USD 9.08 million of payments in the next year. Seasonality matters: retainages build in the first and third quarters and are collected in the second and fourth, and the fourth quarter normally brings the highest operating cash flow, so the nine-month cash flow is not a full-year run rate. EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 65.50% over the last twelve months, but 39.05% if the payables inflow reverses, which is still positive after dividends.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is limited in Government Operations because of capital, licensing, classified designs and clearances, and the Navy fuel plant is the sole provider, which supports renewal and margin; in Commercial Operations competitors such as Framatome, Doosan and AtkinsRéalis bid for work and the margin is 8.29%. The threat of new entrants is low in naval work and moderate in commercial heavy components, where the issuer is the only North American heavy nuclear component manufacturer. Substitutes matter only commercially, where demand depends on the competitiveness of nuclear power against other energy sources. Buyer power is the central force: one customer is 88% of Government Operations revenue, can terminate for convenience and does not have to exercise options, though termination recovers costs and profit on work done. Supplier power is real because single-source suppliers could set price and terms on key materials, which would reduce margin before it reduced volume.

### Macro and policy factors

Policy and regulation are a primary credit driver and the other external factors are not. Appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdown risk set the timing of new awards and payments, the Department of Energy budget drives site-management contracts and their joint-venture income, and nuclear licensing and procurement rules shape both capacity and cost. Executive Order 14372 may restrict distributions by defense contractors that miss performance requirements. Currency is a secondary factor because Canadian operations hold 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment and the issuer hedges with forward contracts of USD 142.5 million notional maturing to December 2028. Tariffs and inflation in steel are noted by the issuer but are not quantified.

### Credit-translated SWOT

The credit-supportive strengths are sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue, liquidity of USD 1.82 billion with no maturity before 2028, low cash interest from zero-coupon convertible debt and government cost recovery on contracts, pensions and decommissioning.

The credit constraints are a margin that has fallen 2.70 percentage points, cash conversion helped by payables timing, an acquisition-led financial policy with no stated leverage target, concentration on one customer and unfunded backlog of 23.03%, and unseen executed documents that leave ranking and covenant definitions unknown.

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are sale proceeds applied to debt, the end of the heightened capital expenditure cycle, a sustained recovery in margin of the kind seen in the third quarter, and conversion of unfunded to funded backlog, which has already lifted funded backlog 28.89% since FY2025.

Threats that could weaken credit quality are a debt-funded acquisition or revolver draw that returns leverage above its FY2025 peak, a continuing resolution or shutdown that delays awards and collections, cost overruns on fixed-price commercial work, and a failed or low-value medical sale.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are scale of USD 3.60 billion of last-twelve-months revenue, sole-source government demand, liquidity of 0.90x gross debt and a distant maturity profile; the main constraints are the margin trend, cash conversion that depends on supplier timing, and an acquisition-led policy whose limits are not documented in the filings supplied. The trend is improving on leverage, with gross leverage down from 3.92x at FY2025 to 3.56x and EBITDA growth of 10.66% over FY2025 in the last twelve months, but deteriorating on margin, and the third quarter suggests stabilisation. Interest cover is high at 13.84x on last-twelve-months cash interest and 17.22x on the contractual interest due in a year. Access to capital markets was shown by the USD 1,250 million convertible issue of 2025, and the only price evidence supplied is the quarter-end fair value of 96.50% of principal for the 2028 senior notes, 95.08% for the 2029 notes and 87.36% for the convertible notes, which does not by itself show stress but is not a market test. The key missing datapoints are the executed documents, the proceeds of the medical sale, the contract-level fixed-price exposure, a rating and market prices.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are funded backlog growth of 28.89% in the nine months of 2026, recognition of about 46% of backlog by the end of 2027, a Navy plan that sustains nuclear procurement, an expected fall in capital expenditure, the third-quarter margin recovery and low cash interest; the headwinds are the fiscal-year funding cycle, integration of Kinectrics, whose controls will be assessed for FY2026, and of Precision Components Group, whose price allocation is preliminary, the pending sale's timing in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, and reversal of payables timing. The 2028 notes become a current liability in 2027, but they are covered by cash. Over three to five years the issues are the 2028, 2029 and 2030 maturities, the convertible notes becoming redeemable from 2028-11-06, the revolver's early-maturity test before the 2030 convertible notes fall due, and the award of unexercised options in 2030 and 2035; the Commercial Operations outlook depends on nuclear utility spending and Canadian refurbishment, and the Government Operations outlook on appropriations.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario that fits this capital structure combines three events. Appropriations for the next federal year are delayed under a continuing resolution while a shutdown risk lingers, new awards slip, and retainage collections and joint-venture dividends that normally arrive in the fourth quarter are delayed. At the same time a fixed-price commercial project overruns and the vendor payments deferred in 2026 are paid, which removes the USD 150.33 million payables inflow. Revenue in Government Operations, which earns 81.43% of segment profit, would fall little because funded backlog is USD 6,585.3 million, but fixed costs of the expanded facilities would be absorbed over fewer awards, so the margin would fall below the nine-month level of 16.46% and last-twelve-months free cash flow would fall towards USD 221.99 million. Liquidity would hold: liquidity of USD 1.82 billion covers 5.39 years of cash interest, capital expenditure and dividends, in total USD 337.34 million a year, even with no operating cash flow at all. The leverage consequence would come from management choices, because a revolver draw for an acquisition before the medical sale closes would lift gross debt from USD 2.02 billion while EBITDA fell. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, and the observable triggers are a fall in funded backlog, a revolver draw, payables falling from USD 281.64 million and a margin below 16.46%.

### Overall credit view

Overall, BWX Technologies presents a strong business profile supported by sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue and a long maturity runway, but credit quality is constrained by a falling EBITDA margin, an acquisition-led financial policy and unseen debt documents. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because conversion of 65.50% is helped by payables timing and capital expenditure remains high. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 and 2029 senior notes being repaid from cash and cash flow or refinanced at par, and on the 2030 convertible notes being addressed before the revolver's early-maturity test applies. The primary downside path is debt-funded acquisitions and margin erosion while government cash timing slips. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, the proceeds and use of the medical sale, contract-level fixed-price data, a rating and market prices. Top risk: acquisition-led leverage.

## Gaps

The executed credit agreement, the three indentures and the supplemental indentures dated 2026-08-07 are not supplied, so the structure of the revolver and the notes, the definitions behind the covenants and the early-maturity test, the restricted-payment and debt baskets and the lien release terms are not established. This limits the structural-priority, covenant and financial-policy conclusions. Severity: High. Action: supply the executed documents and the latest compliance certificate.

The proceeds, tax, size of the retained stake, exact closing date and use of proceeds of the medical business sale, and the revenue and EBITDA of the business, are not stated, so pro forma debt and leverage are not established. This limits the leverage trajectory and the outlook. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the transaction announcement or the closing report.

No rating, traded price or peer set was supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged issuers on a measured basis and market access is judged from the 2025 convertible issue alone. Severity: Medium. Action: supply current ratings, quotes and a peer set if relative work is wanted.

The filings give revenue by contract type but no price ceilings, sharing ratios or estimates at completion, so the overrun exposure on fixed-price work and the extent to which fixed-price incentive contracts behave like cost-plus work are not sized. Severity: Medium. Action: supply contract-level data or management commentary.

The filings give no explanation for the weak fourth-quarter 2025 margin of 13.73%, the third-quarter 2026 shift in Government Operations from firm fixed-price to fixed-price incentive contracts, or the sustainability of the third-quarter margin recovery. Severity: Low. Action: read the next annual report and earnings materials.

No stated leverage target, financial policy or guidance was found, so the financial-policy view rests on documented conduct. Severity: Medium. Action: supply an investor presentation or earnings call transcript.

The share of the pension and retiree medical deficit that government contracts will recover, and the effect of the Kinectrics plan that is open to new participants, are not quantified. Severity: Low. Action: none unless pension work is wanted.

The annual report and first-quarter 2026 report word the lien-release condition on the revolver as one rating from S&P or Moody's at investment grade, while the second- and third-quarter reports require two of three agencies and a stable outlook, with no amendment disclosed, so how soon the revolver could become unsecured is not established. Severity: Low. Action: resolve against the executed credit agreement.

Only nine months of 2026 are reported, so the fourth-quarter retainage collections and joint-venture dividends that normally lift cash flow are not yet visible. Severity: Low. Action: read the FY2026 annual report.
